**Adding a new issue to your GitHub repository**

You can use the following command to add a new issue to your GitHub repository:
```
gh issue add <repo-owner>/<repo-name> --title="<issue-title>" --body="<issue-body>"
```
Replace `<repo-owner>/<repo-name>` with your actual GitHub repository owner and name, `<issue-title>` with the title of the new issue, and `<issue-body>` with the body of the new issue.

For example, if your repository is `johnDoe/myrepo`, and you want to add an issue with the title `Fix bug` and body `The bug is causing the program to crash when trying to open a file`, you would use the following command:
```
gh issue add johnDoe/myrepo --title="Fix bug" --body="The bug is causing the program to crash when trying to open a file"
```
This will add a new issue to your repository with the specified title and body.

You can also use the `search_issues` function to add a new issue. Here's an example:
```
gh issue search --repo=<repo-owner>/<repo-name> --query="<issue-title> <issue-body>"
```
This will search for issues in your GitHub repository that match the specified title and body, and if no matching issues are found, it will create a new issue.

Note that you need to have the `issue` and `search_issues` tools installed and configured on your system to use these commands. If you don't have these tools installed, you can install them using the `gh` command-line tool.
```
gh issue install
```
Also, make sure you have the necessary permissions to add issues to your GitHub repository.
